The bitcoin-watching news service CoinDesk recently released its first quarter look into the cryptocurrency’s performance during the opening months of 2015. Mostly the data is net positive, showing an increase in total wallets, and investment. However, there are a number of included data points that demonstrate slowing growth in key bitcoin, and bitcoin-related areas.
Hows does that correlate with a doubling of number of transactions over the past 12 months, as evidenced by the block chain directly?

Good question. I think combining all of these data points can provide a good overview, but haven't read CoinDesk's report entirely. Transaction volume isn't the greatest metric since it can be manipulated with thousands of small transactions. Blockchain.info provides a couple charts that exclude popular address and chain transactions. Those charts do show an increase, but only 25-50% or so.

Lately PostgreSQL made very huge improvements in terms of performance & features (see links below) and before anything else it's completely FREE. While I appreciate the fact that ASP.net & SQL Server speak natively to each other through LINQ, SQL Server is closed-source, expensive and not so friendly for an open source project like Voat, the only downside is that you need to sacrifice LINQ in order to use PostgreSQL but the efforts will be repaid in the long term, and that's where Voat should aim for! What do you think?

When Voat will become bigger, should it migrate to PostgreSQL?

My experience with PG is that upgrades are very painful and it requires a fair amount of maintenance. So either you risk serious downtime wihle upgrading or have to stick with soon-to-be ancient versions of the database. I've had good experiences with MongoDB for most generic stuff, and specialized databases in addition to that, where feasible. For instance, tabular numeric data in some form of SQL DB, especially when handling money and such, simpler key-value DB's like Redis where speed matters (for instance caches or session data).
